Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does
  - testMath519 builds a monotonically increasing data series of tiny positive values at integer x = 0..26.
  - It creates a GaussianFitter with a LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer, adds all observed points, and calls fitter.fit().
  - The test expects that, during optimization, if the algorithm explores invalid parameter regions (notably negative sigma), GaussianFitter will not let the underlying model throw; instead it should catch such errors and return NaN model values, allowing the optimizer to continue.

- How the fit is wired
  - GaussianFitter.fit() obtains an initial guess and delegates to CurveFitter.fit(...) with a Gaussian.Parametric instance.
  - CurveFitter.fit(...) builds a TheoreticalValuesFunction that, for each observed point, computes f.value(x, params) to feed the optimizer.

- Where the exception comes from
  - Gaussian.Parametric.value(x, params) calls validateParameters(params).
  - validateParameters throws NotStrictlyPositiveException if params[2] (sigma) <= 0.

- Why the exception is not handled
  - TheoreticalValuesFunction.value(...) directly calls f.value(...) for each point and does not catch any exceptions thrown by the model evaluation.
  - When the optimizer (Levenberg-Marquardt) proposes a parameter vector with a non-positive sigma during its iterations (a normal occurrence in unconstrained nonlinear least squares), f.value throws NotStrictlyPositiveException, which propagates out of TheoreticalValuesFunction, through CurveFitter.fit, and out of GaussianFitter.fit.
  - This behavior contradicts the expectation stated in the test comment that “GaussianFitter will catch the raised exceptions and return NaN values instead.”

- Why this dataset triggers the path
  - The supplied data have no clear peak (they monotonically increase), so the optimizer has little guidance and will explore a broad parameter space, including invalid sigma values.
  - Although the initial guess constructed by ParameterGuesser is positive (sigma derived from the x-span fallback is ~11), the optimizer still tries updates with sigma <= 0 during its search.
  - Since there is no protective wrapper around f.value (nor around the Jacobian, if requested), the first such invalid trial causes NotStrictlyPositiveException to be thrown, failing the test.

- Conclusion
  - The failure stems from missing exception handling in the code path that evaluates the model during fitting. Specifically, TheoreticalValuesFunction (used by CurveFitter and thus GaussianFitter) forwards parameter arrays directly to Gaussian.Parametric.value, which enforces sigma > 0 and throws otherwise. Because no catch/translate-to-NaN layer exists, the optimizer cannot continue and the test fails with NotStrictlyPositiveException, contrary to the intended GaussianFitter behavior described in the test.
